title: Hydrogen backside cooling replaces helium in etch and deposition chucks
idea: Box [any | any | any | any | Si | electrostatic-chuck backside gas = 5-15 Torr H2 in a closed loop]: H2 conducts heat better than He (0.18 vs 0.15 W/m-K), so swap the chuck backside gas to H2 below flammability limits, with Pd-membrane return and O2 interlocks.
why: Helium (Qatar offline): backside cooling is a dominant fab He use; H2 matches or beats wafer temperature uniformity at a small fraction of the price and is made on site.

title: Bistable buckled nanobeam storing bits by mechanical position
idea: Po: the bit is a shape. Each cell is a pre-stressed buckled nanobeam (TiN or amorphous carbon) clamped at both ends and resting in one of two curved states; electrostatic pulses from two side electrodes snap it between states, and its position is read by tunnel current to a sense electrode.
why: Facts 1 and 3: no capacitor and no leakage-limited retention, so refresh is zero; risk is snap speed (~ns at 100 nm) and fatigue over 1e15 cycles.

title: Self-clearing capacitor electrodes isolate dielectric breakdown spots
idea: Metallised film capacitors self-heal because a breakdown vaporises the ultra-thin electrode around the fault; make the DRAM pillar's inner electrode a thin oxidisable film (e.g., TiN with a thin Al skin) so a test-time 'clearing' pulse oxidises or opens the electrode locally around a leakage path, turning a dead leaky cell into a slightly smaller working one.
why: Converts dielectric-leakage tail cells into usable cells and lets thinner, higher-k, more defective dielectrics be used for more Cs (facts 1, 3); target ~10x fewer leakage-tail failures.

title: Metal-assisted chemical etching digs 150:1 capacitor holes without plasma
idea: Ideal: holes that dig themselves to any depth. Closest: a DSA-patterned Pt or Ag catalyst mesh sinks into a thick poly-Si mold in HF/H2O2 at room temperature (MacEtch), cutting straight 150:1 holes; the catalyst is stripped, the mold oxidized/lined and used as the capacitor template.
why: Facts 1 and 4: replaces $10M+ cryogenic HAR etchers (and their helium backside cooling) with wet benches; AR 115+ affordable for Cs ~8 fF; capacitor-module capex roughly -40%.
